crime_highlights: The shooter emerged from a vehicle stolen in Prince George
Ms. Dingwall waited in a nearby get-away vehicle to facilitate the escape
Several bullets penetrated the exterior of the dwelling house and were located within the dwelling house
Fortunately, only Lyle Suter sustained physical injury
The shooting took place in the early morning hours (approximately 4:00 a.m.)
rationale_highlights: Gladue factors - Ms. Dingwall's maternal grandmother went through the residential school system and there are significant substance abuse issues in Ms. Dingwall's mother's side of the family
Substance abuse appears to have played a role in Ms. Dingwall's relationship to her co-accused, Kelly Richet, and may have contributed to her role in the offence
the Gladue factors are but one facet to consider within the context of other factors
I conclude that the Gladue factors play a minor role in determining the fit sentence for the firearm offences
note: Court says Gladue factors play only a minor role.

crime_highlights: Mr. Hall threw a non-functioning rifle through the front window of Ms. Mervyn's apartment the following morning
I found that Mr. Hall was the individual who shot at the house multiple times
Ms. Mervyn and Mr. Hall got into a dispute over the phone about the purchase of drugs
rationale_highlights: several generations of his family grew up disconnected from their community, culture and traditions due to a loss of status for marrying a non-native man
his maternal great grandmother, grandmother and his mother experienced racism due to their aboriginal heritage, despite being denied status

In balancing the competing considerations, I give primacy to Mr. Hall's youth, the considerable insight he has demonstrated concerning the negative role alcohol and drugs have had on his life, his significant prospects to fully rehabilitate himself and his aboriginal ancestry
Those considerations lead me to conclude that notwithstanding the serious circumstances of the offence, the mandatory minimum for Count 4 is a fit sentence
note: Crime narrative short; effects on victims limited.
